name: GiddyVaultV3 compound signature covers only the swap payload hash
summary: GiddyVaultV3.compound() authenticates the caller with an EIP-712 signature whose digest binds only keccak256 of each SwapInfo.data field, leaving the accompanying fromToken, toToken, amount and aggregator addresses outside the signed scope. The attacker replayed a signature the operator had already produced, substituted its own token and aggregator parameters, and had the vault route the strategies’ balances out through an aggregator it controlled.
notes: Non-upgradeable contract. The runtime code hash is 0x679791b0c174dd7ef0ebeca701cd4b3e039f8fa100162ec3dcc406d4b5ccf577 both at the deployment block 24923987 and at block 24942491, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

The exploit transaction credits the attacker with 3.531384449443560254 g(yb-tBTC), 6.935949844931976725 g(yb-cbBTC) and 6.274444990265641146 g(yb-WBTC). Six follow-up transactions redeem those shares into yb-tBTC, yb-cbBTC and yb-WBTC and then unwrap them, ending in exactly the three amounts recorded here; the components are therefore the realised BTC-denominated value of the stolen shares rather than a mark on the share tokens themselves. DefiLlama observations are within 130 seconds of the incident timestamp. Nothing was recovered.
